name: Manasseh
charge: Rebuilding the high places; altars to the host of heaven in the temple; passing his sons through the fire; witchcraft; filling Jerusalem with innocent blood
summary: Hezekiah's son undid everything his father had done and more: altars for Baal, a grove, worship of all the host of heaven in both courts of the Lord's house, his children through the fire, observing times, enchantments, familiar spirits, wizards. He shed innocent blood until Jerusalem was filled from one end to another.
offense: Manasseh rebuilt the high places Hezekiah had removed, established idolatrous altars even in the Lord's house, practised forbidden divination, and caused his children to pass through the fire (2 Chronicles 33:1-7). He reversed a reform whose work was visible before him. He also shed innocent blood until Jerusalem was filled from end to end, and led Judah into greater evil than the nations expelled before Israel (2 Kings 21:9, 16). The Lord spoke to him and his people, but they would not hear (2 Chronicles 33:10). Authority amplified his departure by making it the nation's course.
judgment: The Lord brought the captains of the host of Assyria, who took Manasseh among the thorns, bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon. There he humbled himself greatly and prayed; the Prayer of Manasseh preserves the tradition of it. God brought him back to his kingdom and he took away the strange gods. But the sentence on Judah for his sins stood: the Lord would not pardon.
offenseFull: Manasseh rebuilt the high places Hezekiah had removed, established idolatrous altars even in the Lord's house, practised forbidden divination, and caused his children to pass through the fire (2 Chronicles 33:1-7). He reversed a reform whose work was visible before him.

He also shed innocent blood until Jerusalem was filled from end to end, and led Judah into greater evil than the nations expelled before Israel (2 Kings 21:9, 16). The Lord spoke to him and his people, but they would not hear (2 Chronicles 33:10). Authority amplified his departure by making it the nation's course.

entries.commentary: Manasseh begins to reign at twelve years old and reigns fifty-five years, doing evil after the abominations of the heathen the Most High cast out before Israel. He rebuilds the high places Hezekiah destroyed, rears altars for Baal, makes a grove as Ahab did, and worships the host of heaven, even building altars in the house of the Most High where He set His name; this is a wickedness with zero fear of the Most High. The people did not serve idols for nothing but for the self-gratification in it, the same as men today keep pagan feasts for the gifts, the food, and the reveling, not for what the day claims to be. He makes his son pass through the fire, observes times, uses enchantments, and deals with familiar spirits and wizards, provoking the Most High to anger, and seduces Judah to do more evil than the nations the Most High destroyed. Repentance is always possible; our people are repenting, not repented, so no man should judge before the time who is or is not of the two-thirds. Continue in the work of the Most High and let Christ judge in the end.

The Most High speaks by His servants the prophets that because Manasseh did wickedly above all the Amorites and made Judah to sin, He is bringing such evil upon Jerusalem that both ears of whoever hears it shall tingle. He will stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria and the plummet of the house of Ahab, and wipe Jerusalem as a man wipes a dish and turns it upside down; the same desolation done to Samaria will reach Judah. He will forsake the remnant of His inheritance and deliver them into the hand of their enemies to be a prey and a spoil, because they have provoked Him to anger since the day their fathers came out of Egypt. The Most High has borne with this wickedness for hundreds of years. -

Manasseh sheds innocent blood very much, filling Jerusalem from one end to the other, beside the sin with which he made Judah to sin. His remaining acts are written in the chronicles of the kings of Judah, and the prayer of Manasseh is recorded in the Apocrypha, prayed while he was held captive in Babylon. Chronicles shows the captains of the king of Assyria took Manasseh among the thorns and carried him with fetters to Babylon, then a province under Assyria; there he repented and prayed. The history shows a power struggle beginning, where Assyrian kings ruled over Babylon, and later Babylonian kings ruled over Assyria; Manasseh sleeps with his fathers and Amon his son reigns. -

Amon begins to reign at twenty-two years old and reigns two years, doing evil as his father Manasseh did, walking in all his ways and serving the idols his father served. He forsakes the Most High God of his fathers and walks not in His way. His own servants conspire against him and slay him in his house; the people of the land slay the conspirators and make Josiah his son king in his stead.

Manasseh begins to reign at twelve years old and reigns fifty five years in Jerusalem, but he does that which is evil in the sight of the Lord, after the abominations of the heathen the Most High had cast out before the children of Israel. He rebuilds the high places his father Hezekiah had broken down, rears up altars for Baal, makes groves, and worships all the host of heaven and serves them. He builds altars even in the house of the Lord, the very place of which the Most High had said, In Jerusalem shall my name be for ever.

He builds altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord, and causes his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom, which is child sacrifice, the same spirit as abortion today. He observes times, uses enchantments, uses witchcraft, and deals with a familiar spirit and with wizards, working much evil to provoke the Most High to anger. Every one of these things is a commandment he broke. He sets a carved idol in the house of God, the very house of which the Most High said to David and Solomon, In this house and in Jerusalem will I put my name for ever, and Manasseh makes Judah do worse than the heathen the Lord destroyed before them. -

The Most High speaks to Manasseh and his people, but they will not hearken, so he brings upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria. They take Manasseh among the thorns, bind him with chains, and carry him to Babylon. The kings of Israel that were once kings are brought down into captivity, exactly as the curses warned. -

When he is in affliction, Manasseh beseeches the Lord his God and humbles himself greatly before the God of his fathers, and prays unto him. The Most High is entreated of him, hears his supplication, and brings him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom, and then Manasseh knows that the Lord he was God. This is the pattern of [2 Chronicles 7:14](/bible/2-chronicles/7#v14), that a people called by his name who humble themselves will be heard.

After this he builds a wall for the city of David, sets captains of war in the fenced cities of Judah, and takes away the strange gods and the idol out of the house of the Lord, casting them out of the city. He repairs the altar of the Lord, sacrifices peace offerings and thank offerings on it, and commands Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel, though the people still sacrifice in the high places, only unto the Lord their God. -

The rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer unto his God, are written in the book of the kings of Israel, and his prayer and how the Most High was entreated of him are written among the sayings of the seers. This is the prayer of Manasseh, a writing of the Apocrypha found before the Maccabees, which is part of the Bible. Manasseh sleeps with his fathers and Amon his son reigns in his stead. -

Amon is twenty two years old when he begins to reign and reigns two years in Jerusalem, doing evil in the sight of the Lord as Manasseh his father, sacrificing to all the carved images Manasseh had made. But Amon does not humble himself before the Lord as his father had humbled himself; instead he trespasses more and more, and his own servants conspire against him and slay him in his house. The people of the land slay the conspirators and make Josiah his son king in his stead. A sentence not executed speedily set his heart to do more evil, and his sins abounded to his own destruction. -

Josiah gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem, went up to the house of the Most High with the priests, the prophets, and all the people both small and great, and read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that was found there. Our forefathers had the Bible; the king read it openly, then stood by a pillar and made a covenant before the Lord to walk after him and keep his commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all their heart and soul. All the people stood to the covenant to perform the words written in the book. -

The king commanded Hilkiah and the priests to bring out of the temple all the vessels made for Baal, for the grove, and for all the host of heaven, and he burned them in the fields of Kidron and carried their ashes to Bethel. He put down the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places and around Jerusalem, and those that burnt incense to Baal, to the sun, the moon, the planets, and all the host of heaven. When Josiah read the law the fear of the Lord came upon him and he saw why the nation was under judgment, just as a person is cut when they first hear the truth and realize what they have been doing wrong. -

He brought the grove out of the house of the Lord to the brook Kidron, burned it, stamped it to powder, and cast the powder on the graves of the children of the people. He broke down the houses of the sodomites that were by the house of the Lord, where the women wove hangings for the grove; there should be no sodomite among the sons of Israel, yet they had grown so bold as to do this wickedness right beside the temple. He brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where they had burnt incense, and though the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar, they still ate of the unleavened bread among their brethren.

Josiah defiled Topheth in the valley of the children of Hinnom so that no man might make his son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech. Topheth was the place where the people sacrificed their children, and it had to be defiled because Israel would not stop the evil on its own. -

He took away the horses the kings of Judah had given to the sun and burnt the chariots of the sun with fire. He beat down the altars on the roof of Ahaz's chamber and the altars Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, and cast their dust into the brook Kidron. He defiled the high places Solomon had built for Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom, the abominations of the Zidonians, Moabites, and Ammonites, and broke in pieces the images, cut down the groves, and filled their places with the bones of men. This is repentance in action: cleaning house, getting rid of every idol and evil that causes a people to go off from the Lord and to fall under punishment. -

Josiah also destroyed the altar and high place at Bethel that Jeroboam had made when he set up the golden calves, burning it and stamping it small to powder. Turning himself, he spied the sepulchres in the mount, took out the bones, and burnt them upon the altar to pollute it, according to the word the man of God had proclaimed. When told which sepulchre belonged to the man of God who prophesied these things, he said to let him alone and let no man move his bones. -

Josiah also took away all the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord to anger, and did to them as he had done at Bethel. The northern kingdom had already been carried into captivity by Assyria, so most of the people were gone, yet the idolatrous houses remained. He slew all the priests of the high places upon their altars, burnt men's bones upon them, and returned to Jerusalem.

The king commanded all the people to keep the Passover to the Lord their God as it is written in the book of this covenant. Such a Passover had not been held from the days of the judges nor in all the days of the kings of Israel and Judah, but in the eighteenth year of Josiah this Passover was held in Jerusalem. Reading the book of the law brought the nation back to keeping the appointed feasts in order, just as the feast is kept in order today. -

Josiah also put away the workers with familiar spirits, the wizards, the images, the idols, and all the abominations spied in Judah and Jerusalem, that he might perform the words of the law found by Hilkiah. There was no king before or after him that turned to the Lord with all his heart, soul, and might according to all the law of Moses; he put things in order like a true leader. Nevertheless the Lord did not turn from the fierceness of his great wrath because of the provocations of Manasseh, and said he would remove Judah out of his sight as he had removed Israel and cast off Jerusalem.

Pharaohnechoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates, and Josiah went against him and was slain at Megiddo. Josiah got involved in a matter that did not concern him and lost his life in it, a warning not to enter into quarrels that are not one's own. His servants carried him dead in a chariot from Megiddo to Jerusalem and buried him, and the people took Jehoahaz his son and anointed him king in his father's place.

Jehoahaz was twenty three years old and reigned three months in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all his fathers had done. Pharaohnechoh bound him at Riblah so he might not reign, put the land to a tribute of silver and gold, and made Eliakim the son of Josiah king, turning his name to Jehoiakim. Jehoiakim taxed the people to pay Pharaoh, exacting the silver and gold of every man of the land, and he also did evil in the sight of the Lord like his forefathers, not like his father Josiah.

In Jehoiakim's days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant three years, then turned and rebelled against him. The Lord sent bands of the Chaldeans, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites against Judah to destroy it according to the word he spake by his prophets. This came upon Judah at the commandment of the Lord to remove them out of his sight for the sins of Manasseh and the innocent blood he shed, which the Lord would not pardon. -

Jehoiakim slept with his fathers and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place. The king of Egypt came no more out of his land, for the king of Babylon had taken all that pertained to Egypt from the river of Egypt to the river Euphrates. Babylon took over as had been prophesied throughout the Bible, in Daniel and in Jeremiah, that Nebuchadnezzar would ransack Jerusalem and the surrounding lands.

Jehoiachin was eighteen years old and reigned three months in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all his fathers had done. The servants of Nebuchadnezzar came up against Jerusalem and besieged it, and the king himself came against the city while it was besieged. Jehoiachin went out to the king of Babylon with his mother, servants, princes, and officers, and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

Nebuchadnezzar carried out all the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, and cut in pieces the vessels of gold Solomon had made, as the Lord had said. He carried away all Jerusalem, all the princes, all the mighty men of valour, ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths, leaving only the poorest of the people of the land. He carried Jehoiachin, the king's mother, wives, and officers to Babylon, along with the men of might and craftsmen and smiths, wanting them to build for him what they had built in their own land, as conquering nations always used Israel's skill and industry. -

The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's father's brother, king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah. Zedekiah was twenty one years old and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all Jehoiakim had done. Through the anger of the Lord it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had cast them out of his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. -

Though Moses and Samuel stood before Him, the mind of the Most High could not be toward this people; He says cast them out of My sight. When the people ask where they shall go, the answer is such as are for death to death, for the sword to the sword, for the famine to the famine, and for the captivity to the captivity. That is how we got removed from before the Most High.

He appoints four kinds over them: the sword to slay, the dogs to tear, and the fowls and beasts to devour, and He will remove them into all kingdoms of the earth because of what Manasseh son of Hezekiah did in Jerusalem. He is weary with repenting and will bereave them of children because they return not from their ways; the mother of young men gets a spoiler at noonday, and she that bore seven languishes and gives up the ghost. That hit home; there was a sister last sabbath who had seven sons and was very much depressed. The scripture speaks to a real grief among the people.

Jeremiah cries woe over being born a man of strife and contention, cursed by everyone though he lent to no one on usury. The Most High answers that it shall be well with his remnant. That remnant is those who are keeping the commandments. Their substance and treasures will be given to the spoil for all their sins, and they will pass with their enemies into a land they do not know.

Jeremiah asks the Most High to remember him, visit him, and revenge him of his persecutors, and not to take him away in His longsuffering, since for His sake he has suffered rebuke. His words were found and Jeremiah did eat them, and they were the joy and rejoicing of his heart, for he is called by the name of the Most High and sat alone, filled with indignation. He asks why his pain is perpetual and his wound refuses to be healed. This is what the prophets go through: we bring healing, order, structure and discipline to our people and get hated and treated badly, and sometimes these are the thoughts we have.

If Jeremiah returns, the Most High will bring him again to stand before Him; if he takes the precious from the vile he shall be as His mouth. Let them return to him, but he is not to return to them. He will make Jeremiah a fenced brazen wall; they shall fight against him but not prevail, for the Most High is with him to save and deliver him. That is what we live on. When we go out teaching this bible, and when brothers and sisters apply the commandments to their everyday lives, people will come against us, but the Most High is our defense. As long as we keep the commandments and the faith of Christ, no one can prevail, and if they try they will fail. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

verses.text: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and reigned fifty and five years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Hephzi–bah.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, after the abominations of the heathen, whom the Lord cast out before the children of Israel.

For he built up again the high places which Hezekiah his father had destroyed; and he reared up altars for Baal, and made a grove, as did Ahab king of Israel; and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them.
And he built altars in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord said, In Jerusalem will I put my name.
And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.

And he made his son pass through the fire, and observed times, and used enchantments, and dealt with familiar spirits and wizards: he wrought much wickedness in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.

And he set a graven image of the grove that he had made in the house, of which the Lord said to David, and to Solomon his son, In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all tribes of Israel, will I put my name for ever:

Neither will I make the feet of Israel move any more out of the land which I gave their fathers; only if they will observe to do according to all that I have commanded them, and according to all the law that my servant Moses commanded them.
But they hearkened not: and Manasseh seduced them to do more evil than did the nations whom the Lord destroyed before the children of Israel.
And the Lord spake by his servants the prophets, saying,
Because Manasseh king of Judah hath done these abominations, and hath done wickedly above all that the Amorites did, which were before him, and hath made Judah also to sin with his idols:
Therefore thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Behold, I am bringing such evil upon Jerusalem and Judah, that whosoever heareth of it, both his ears shall tingle.
And I will stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria, and the plummet of the house of Ahab: and I will wipe Jerusalem as a man wipeth a dish, wiping it, and turning it upside down.
And I will forsake the remnant of mine inheritance, and deliver them into the hand of their enemies; and they shall become a prey and a spoil to all their enemies;
Because they have done that which was evil in my sight, and have provoked me to anger, since the day their fathers came forth out of Egypt, even unto this day.

Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood very much, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another; beside his sin wherewith he made Judah to sin, in doing that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty and five years in Jerusalem:
But did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, like unto the abominations of the heathen, whom the Lord had cast out before the children of Israel.
For he built again the high places which Hezekiah his father had broken down, and he reared up altars for Baalim, and made groves, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them.
Also he built altars in the house of the Lord, whereof the Lord had said, In Jerusalem shall my name be for ever.
And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.

And he caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom: also he observed times, and used enchantments, and used witchcraft, and dealt with a familiar spirit, and with wizards: he wrought much evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.

And he set a carved image, the idol which he had made, in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen before all the tribes of Israel, will I put my name for ever:

Neither will I any more remove the foot of Israel from out of the land which I have appointed for your fathers; so that they will take heed to do all that I have commanded them, according to the whole law and the statutes and the ordinances by the hand of Moses.
So Manasseh made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, and to do worse than the heathen, whom the Lord had destroyed before the children of Israel.
And the Lord spake to Manasseh, and to his people: but they would not hearken.
Wherefore the Lord brought upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, which took Manasseh among the thorns, and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.
And when he was in affliction, he besought the Lord his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers,
And prayed unto him: and he was intreated of him, and heard his supplication, and brought him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the Lord he was God.
Notwithstanding the Lord turned not from the fierceness of his great wrath, wherewith his anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations that Manasseh had provoked him withal.
Surely at the commandment of the Lord came this upon Judah, to remove them out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he did;
And also for the innocent blood that he shed: for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; which the Lord would not pardon.
And I will cause them to be removed into all kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh the son of Hezekiah king of Judah, for that which he did in Jerusalem.

I am bowed down with many iron bands, that I cannot lift up mine head, neither have any release: for I have provoked thy wrath, and done evil before thee: I did not thy will, neither kept I thy commandments: I have set up abominations, and have multiplied offences.
Now therefore I bow the knee of mine heart, beseeching thee of grace.
I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned, and I acknowledge mine iniquities:

wherefore, I humbly beseech thee, forgive me, O Lord, forgive me, and destroy me not with mine iniquites. Be not angry with me for ever, by reserving evil for me; neither condemn me to the lower parts of the earth. For thou art the God, even the God of them that repent;
and in me thou wilt shew all thy goodness: for thou wilt save me, that am unworthy, according to thy great mercy.

lawsResolved.text: You shall not engage in idolatry and worship or serve the gods, idols or graven images of other nations.
are commanded to destroy all pagan idols, shrines, alters, groves, pillars, images, etc., that are in the land.
You shall not let any of your offspring pass through the fire of Molech.
A man or a woman with a familiar spirit or who is a wizard shall be put to death.
Divination, soothsaying, and the use of mediums, spiritists and occultists are forbidden practices.
Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
Confession and repentance necessary to pardon sin and for God to release us from His chastisements and punishments.

Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood very much, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another; beside his sin wherewith he made Judah to sin, in doing that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty and five years in Jerusalem:
But did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, like unto the abominations of the heathen, whom the Lord had cast out before the children of Israel.
For he built again the high places which Hezekiah his father had broken down, and he reared up altars for Baalim, and made groves, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them.
Also he built altars in the house of the Lord, whereof the Lord had said, In Jerusalem shall my name be for ever.
And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.

And he caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom: also he observed times, and used enchantments, and used witchcraft, and dealt with a familiar spirit, and with wizards: he wrought much evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.

And he set a carved image, the idol which he had made, in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen before all the tribes of Israel, will I put my name for ever:

Neither will I any more remove the foot of Israel from out of the land which I have appointed for your fathers; so that they will take heed to do all that I have commanded them, according to the whole law and the statutes and the ordinances by the hand of Moses.
So Manasseh made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, and to do worse than the heathen, whom the Lord had destroyed before the children of Israel.
And the Lord spake to Manasseh, and to his people: but they would not hearken.
Wherefore the Lord brought upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, which took Manasseh among the thorns, and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.
And when he was in affliction, he besought the Lord his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers,
And prayed unto him: and he was intreated of him, and heard his supplication, and brought him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the Lord he was God.
Notwithstanding the Lord turned not from the fierceness of his great wrath, wherewith his anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations that Manasseh had provoked him withal.
Surely at the commandment of the Lord came this upon Judah, to remove them out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he did;
And also for the innocent blood that he shed: for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; which the Lord would not pardon.
And I will cause them to be removed into all kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh the son of Hezekiah king of Judah, for that which he did in Jerusalem.

I am bowed down with many iron bands, that I cannot lift up mine head, neither have any release: for I have provoked thy wrath, and done evil before thee: I did not thy will, neither kept I thy commandments: I have set up abominations, and have multiplied offences.
Now therefore I bow the knee of mine heart, beseeching thee of grace.
I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned, and I acknowledge mine iniquities:

wherefore, I humbly beseech thee, forgive me, O Lord, forgive me, and destroy me not with mine iniquites. Be not angry with me for ever, by reserving evil for me; neither condemn me to the lower parts of the earth. For thou art the God, even the God of them that repent;
and in me thou wilt shew all thy goodness: for thou wilt save me, that am unworthy, according to thy great mercy.
